back: Volcanic outgassing
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

front: What is the term for carbon carried into the mantle when oceanic plates sink?
back: Subduction
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

front: Through which part of the Earth system does the fast carbon cycle mainly move carbon?

subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

front: Through which part of the Earth system does the slow carbon cycle mainly move carbon?
back: Rocks (the lithosphere), over millions of years
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

front: What is the biological pump?

subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

front: What are the microscopic plants at the ocean surface that photosynthesise called?
back: Phytoplankton
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: Dead organic particles sinking from the surface ocean to the deep sea
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: CO2 dissolves in cold surface water, which sinks and carries carbon to the deep ocean
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: Gases are more soluble in colder water
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

front: What is the carbonate pump?
back: Marine organisms make calcium carbonate shells that sink and form sediments
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: Outgassing
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: The balance of carbon inputs to and outputs from the stores

back: Regrowing plants take up CO2 by photosynthesis over years to decades

back: Carbon dioxide (and water vapour)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: Cement production

subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: It exposes soil organic matter to oxygen, speeding decomposition

back: Cattle (livestock) farming
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: Soil carbon falls as inputs from litter drop and soils erode

back: Vegetation and soil are covered by concrete, reducing carbon storage
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Paper 1: Physical geography::Water and carbon cycles::3.1.1.3 The carbon cycle

back: It makes it harder to build calcium carbonate shells and skeletons

back: 1 Gt (both are 10¹⁵ grams)

back: Parts per million, the number of CO2 molecules per million air molecules

back: 2 cumecs

front: Peak rainfall is at 10:00 and peak discharge at 16:00. What is the lag time?
back: 6 hours

front: On a hydrograph, which type of graph usually shows rainfall?
back: A bar graph (with discharge as a line graph)

front: Which simple field method measures surface velocity of a stream?

front: Why is a float velocity reading multiplied by about 0.8?
back: Surface flow is faster than the average flow of the whole channel

front: Which field instrument gives a more accurate measure of stream velocity than a float?
back: A flow meter (impeller)

front: Which field method measures how fast water soaks into the ground?
back: An infiltration ring (cylinder infiltrometer)

front: How can interception be measured in the field?

front: Why is a moving average used on rainfall data?

front: Why is a logarithmic scale useful for showing carbon store sizes?
